explanations.explanation: That's one of the three, baker. The LORD tells Moses, "Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is defiled by a dead body." (Numbers 5:2) Skin disease leads the list, so that's the one on this card. Three groups in one verse, and you found the first one.

Debt is a sneaky pick, friend, because it sounds like trouble in a camp. But it's not on the LORD's list. He names anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone defiled by a dead body (Numbers 5:2). Nobody gets sent outside over an unpaid bill here. I've owed a few quarters in my day myself, and I'm still standing.

I get why this one tempts you, but the LORD never says it. His list in Numbers 5:2 is anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone defiled by a dead body. Where a person was born isn't on it. The command is about those three things and nothing else.

Careful, friend, this one has a trap with the word "only." The LORD says, "You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp…" (Numbers 5:3) So the command covers men AND women. Leaving the women out is like handing out cookies to half the room and wondering why the other half is staring at you.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp…" (Numbers 5:3) So it isn't only the men. Women are included too. One little word like "only" can sneak right past you, and you caught it.

explanations.answer: So they won't defile the camp where He lives
explanations.explanation: That's the reason He gives. The LORD says to send them outside "so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." (Numbers 5:3) The camp is where He dwells among them, and that's what the command is about. You read the verse right, baker.

explanations.answer: So they won't disturb the camp while it rests
explanations.explanation: Resting does sound like a camp thing, but the LORD never says it. His words are that they go outside "so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." (Numbers 5:3) The reason is the camp being defiled, where He dwells. Nothing in the verse is about noise or naps. No snooze button involved.

explanations.answer: So they won't delay the camp when it moves
explanations.explanation: Moving day is a fair guess, but it's not the reason in the verse. The LORD says they are sent out "so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." (Numbers 5:3) He talks about defiling the camp, not slowing it down. Nobody's running late for a camp schedule here.

explanations.answer: Leave the camp for a week
explanations.explanation: Leaving the camp is in this passage, but it belongs to the first part, about skin disease, discharge and dead bodies (Numbers 5:2-3). For the person who wronged someone, verse 7 says he "must confess the sin he has committed." No week away is mentioned. Confession is the first step.

Double is a big jump, friend. The verse says, "He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value…" (Numbers 5:7) So it's the full value plus a fifth, not twice the value. That's a lot less than double, though it still adds up.

Half is too much. The verse says, "He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value…" (Numbers 5:7) A fifth is smaller than a half. Think of cutting one cookie into five pieces and adding one piece, not two and a half.
